item.title: Mount Aso and Nakadake Crater — Guide
item.description: Mount Aso (Aso-san), in the centre of Kumamoto, is one of the world’s most active volcanoes and the beating heart of the region. It sits within one of the largest volcanic calderas on Earth — a vast basin, formed by ancient super-eruptions, that today holds towns, farms and railways ringed by the caldera’s grassy rim. At its centre rise five volcanic peaks, of which Nakadake is still highly active. When conditions allow, visitors can go right up to the rim of Nakadake’s crater and peer down at a steaming, otherworldly turquoise pool of volcanic water, ringed by barren ash-grey slopes and rising fumes — a raw, unforgettable sight found in few other places.
